root_cause.text: The kexec code on powerpc fails to temporarily re-enable SMT before waking offline CPUs, so `add_cpu()` fails because `cpu_bootable()` returns false for non-primary threads when SMT is disabled or partially enabled.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states "add_cpu() fails due to cpu_bootable() returning false for CPUs that fail the cpu_smt_thread_allowed() check or non primary threads if SMT is disabled." The patch fixes this by adding `kexec_smt_reenable()` which sets `cpu_smt_num_threads = threads_per_core` and `cpu_smt_control = CPU_SMT_ENABLED` before calling `wake_offline_cpus()`.

vuln_statements.explanation: This loop iterates over all present CPUs, and for each offline CPU, it will attempt to wake it. However, no SMT re-enable is performed before this loop, so add_cpu() fails for non-primary threads because cpu_bootable() returns false when SMT is disabled.

This condition selects offline CPUs for wake-up. The subsequent wake-up call (add_cpu) will fail because cpu_bootable() returns false for non-primary threads when SMT is disabled or partially enabled.
This log message is printed before the wake-up attempt, but no SMT re-enable has been performed, leading to failure as add_cpu() will be called without the necessary SMT condition.
This variable declaration is part of the loop that iterates over CPUs to wake them without re-enabling SMT, which is necessary for cpu_bootable() to return true for non-primary threads.

This memory barrier is part of the CPU wake-up sequence (e.g., after writing to the spin table). The missing SMT re-enable before this barrier causes the wake-up to fail for non-primary threads because cpu_bootable() returns false.
